title: Empowering Vector Architectures for ML: The CAMP Architecture for Matrix Multiplication
problem: Existing vector architectures (VAs) and SIMD units—including ARM SVE and RISC-V SIMD—cannot efficiently execute quantized neural network (QNN) matrix multiplication at 4-bit and 8-bit integer precisions because their datapaths are designed for wider, fixed-width computations.
motivation: Quantized models (4-bit and 8-bit) are the dominant deployment format for LLMs and CNNs at the edge and on server platforms, yet the gap between quantized arithmetic efficiency and what vector ISAs provide forces inefficient emulation that wastes throughput and energy.
method: CAMP introduces a specialized multiplier that breaks down quantized integer multiplication (operations using reduced-precision 4-bit and 8-bit integers) through a two-level nested approach using Cartesian products—decomposing each multiplication into smaller sub-multiplications. This design efficiently handles multiple precision levels (4-bit and 8-bit integers) within the same circuit by recognizing and exploiting the mathematical patterns in quantized matrix operations. CAMP was integrated into the ARM A64FX processor (using ARMv8 SVE, fabricated at TSMC 7 nm) and RISC-V edge SoCs (fabricated at GlobalFoundries 22 nm), increasing chip area by 1% and 4% respectively.
key_novelty: CAMP, a hierarchical multiplier that uses Cartesian products (breaking large multiplications into smaller nested operations), enables vector architectures to efficiently execute multiple precision levels (4-bit and 8-bit) of quantized neural network matrix multiplication with just 1-4% chip area overhead.
contributions: CAMP architecture: a hybrid multiplier extending VA/SIMD datapaths to natively support INT4 and INT8 GEMM
Up to 17x performance improvement over ARM A64FX baseline for matrix multiply operations
Up to 23x performance improvement over a RISC-V edge SoC baseline
Area overhead of only 1% (ARM TSMC 7nm) and 4% (RISC-V GF22nm) verified through place-and-route

metrics.speedup: up to 17x over ARM A64FX; up to 23x over RISC-V SoC for quantized matrix multiply
metrics.area: 1% overhead at TSMC 7nm (ARM); 4% overhead at GF22nm (RISC-V)

primary_theme: quantized GEMM acceleration in vector/SIMD architectures
